messages.author: a38e579a8decc4d1
messages.subject: inla.posterior.sample
parts:
Hi,

The current version of this function (from the July 4 inla version) seems to have some strange behaviour.  Here is a fairly minimal example plotting samples from the joint marginal of the hyperparameters of the ar1 part of a model: 

n = 1000
rho = 0.8
prec = 10
eta = as.vector(arima.sim(list(order = c(1,0,0), ar = rho), n = n,sd=sqrt(1/prec)))
y=rpois(n,10*exp(eta))
data = list(y=y,z=1:n)
formula = y~f(z,model="ar1")
result = inla(formula,family="poisson", data = data, control.compute=list(config=TRUE))
nsim <- 1000
sample <- inla.posterior.sample(nsim,result)
x <- matrix(NA,nsim,2)
for (i in 1:nsim) x[i,] <- sample[[i]]$hyperpar
plot(x)

So, the sample just contain 9 unique values for the hyperparameters.  I suppose this is not intended behaviour?  

Best regards,
Jarle

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample
parts:
It is expected when using the CCD design for the integration over \theta. You can use change it by
 control.inla=list(int.strategy='grid', dz=0.2)
or, easiest, is to use the inla.hyperpar() function as
  result = inla.hyperpar(result, dz=0.5) ### smaller dz implies finer grid
and the use it

best,
Elias

messages.author: a38e579a8decc4d1
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample
parts:
Thanks for the help.

We need samples from the joint posterior of everything because we are interested in some parameters which are nonlinear functions of both the latent parameters and the hyperparameters.

What we try to do is to implement a lognormal prior on one the negative value of one of the fixed effects (the regression coefficient for quadratic effect of one of the covariates) (this makes some sense in the biological context).  So we use rejection sampling to modify the output form inla.posterior.sample such that it corresponds to our desired choice of lognormal prior.  This works ok as the the lognormal is not too vague.

Jarle

that would work, yes.

in order to have a finer resolution of the hyperparameter, you have to,
as Elias write, increase the number of integration points (in one way or
another), as only those are used in inla.posterior.sample() [for
computational speed reasons...]
